attempts.bug_summary: When both horizontal metric tables are present on the TrueType path, the horizontal metrics parser is given the header-table descriptor instead of the metrics-table descriptor. This produces incorrect glyph advance widths for fonts whose hhea and hmtx tables are located or structured differently.

In the CFF-table parsing path, the optional `maxp` table is processed only when a `name` table is also present. As a result, valid CFF fonts that provide glyph-count information but omit naming metadata retain an unset `numGlyphs` value.

The TrueType path now checks for the maxp table before reading indexToLocFormat from the head table. When maxp is absent and the head-table read would otherwise fail, this changes the observable exception and operation order from the specified stream failure to an immediate missing-table exception.

Composite-object coordinates are scaled again before the composite-boundary adjustment. This causes points with both a non-unit scale and a composite boundary to receive an unintended second scaling, while other processing paths remain unchanged.

When a cubic path point is processed with a non-legacy CTM, its third coordinate is transformed from the second control point instead of its own source coordinates. As a result, `B` points with distinct third coordinates produce an incorrect final control point only when CTM processing is active.

Arc radii are additionally multiplied by the non-legacy coordinate scale when both CTM processing and a non-unit scale are active. The endpoint follows the normal CTM and scale pipeline, but the radii incorrectly acquire scale-dependent values even though only legacy processing should scale them.

When both DeltaX and DeltaY are present, the DeltaY reuse boundary is derived from the DeltaX list length instead of the DeltaY list length. This causes DeltaY values to repeat too early or can produce an out-of-bounds access when the two lists have different lengths.

When both the text CTM and composite-object CTM are configured, the method reuses the text CTM for the post-adjustment composite transformation instead of applying the composite CTM. This produces incorrect final coordinates only for combined CTM configurations, while configurations using either transformation alone remain unaffected.

When both a text CTM and a non-unit scale are used, the text origin is scaled before CTM transformation and then scaled again before boundary adjustment. This causes CTM-transformed origins to receive the scale factor twice, while untransformed coordinates retain the normal behavior.

The RGBA parser derives the alpha component from the final comma-separated value rather than consistently using the fourth component. Inputs with additional comma-separated values therefore produce an incorrect alpha value instead of using the specified fourth value.

The fallback decoding path strips the sign from a signed hash-prefixed color before calling `Color.decode`. Inputs using a leading plus together with the `#` radix prefix can therefore fail decoding even though `Color.decode` supports that representation.

The rgb component parser uses Java's base-detecting integer decoder rather than the decimal parser required for comma-separated RGB components. Consequently, components with leading zeroes are interpreted as octal values, or may throw for digits invalid in octal notation, even though they are valid decimal RGB values.

The unequal-border rendering path uses the bottom border width when positioning the top border vertically. This produces an incorrect top-border boundary whenever the top and bottom border widths differ, while leaving uniform-border cases unaffected.

When unequal left and right borders are rendered, the right-border object uses the opposite side's width and offset source. This produces an incorrectly positioned and sized right border when the horizontal border widths differ, while uniform and top/bottom-only configurations remain unaffected.

When a border dash pattern and element opacity are configured together, border dash processing is skipped because the dash pattern is treated as applicable only to fully opaque borders. The borders are still created with their configured widths and alpha, but their line styling becomes solid instead of dashed.

When a span is both explicitly assigned a weight and marked bold, the renderer applies the generic bold weight instead of preserving the explicit weight. Spans with only one of these attributes continue to render normally.

attempts.bug_summary: When an underlined span has no explicit underline width, the fallback width is derived from the line height rather than the span's font size. This produces incorrectly sized underlines when line spacing or another span causes the line height to differ from the underlined span's font size.

When a line contains a placeholder span, its width is applied only for left-aligned lines. For centered or right-aligned lines, subsequent rendered spans are positioned as though the placeholder occupied no horizontal space, causing overlap and incorrect placement.

attempts.bug_summary: Intermediate-page paired annotations use the current page's ratio source for the second displayed half instead of the preceding adjacent pair. This affects documents with non-uniform cutting ratios while leaving equal-ratio and ratio-free cases unchanged.

When the stamp is configured for the left side, a non-empty cutting-ratio list incorrectly takes precedence over an explicitly configured vertical offset. As a result, left-side appearances are vertically centered instead of using the supplied offset only when both settings are present.

attempts.bug_summary: The filter detected the prior mutation because the test combines Side.Left, a non-empty cutting-ratio list, and an explicit offset; the altered condition forced vertical centering, producing 40.0 instead of the configured 7.0. This version instead derives the right-edge position of an intermediate left-side annotation from the preceding page's width, so it is incorrect only when adjacent pages have different widths.

When clipNumber is active in the horizontal-edge branch, clip positions use the remainder-group size as the modulus throughout the initial groups instead of the configured clip count. This produces incorrect repeated clip positions when the page count is not evenly divisible by clipNumber.

When a bottom-edge stamp uses an active clipNumber together with an explicit offset, the horizontal position is centered instead of honoring the configured offset. This incorrect interaction between the side, clipping configuration, and offset affects only that combined configuration; other horizontal placements retain their normal behavior.
